# Savings banks, credit and consumer cooperatives (`cooperatives_savings_banks`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/economy.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Economy & finance (`economy`)
- Deps: helped by banking_credit, double_entry
- Core idea: Savings bank: accepts very small deposits from labourers and servants, pays a modest safe interest, invests in public bonds, run by unpaid trustees without shareholders. Credit cooperative (Raiffeisen): villagers pool savings and lend to one another, all members liable for its debts; because neighbours know who is reliable and watch how the loan is used, they can lend to the poor without collateral. Consumer cooperative (Rochdale 1844): members own the shop, sell pure goods at market prices for cash only, and share any surplus in proportion to purchases, one member one vote. All three give people of small means credit and savings outside the moneylender.
- Pitfalls:
  - Selling below cost or giving credit in a co-op shop: it goes bankrupt
  - Letting a savings bank chase high returns with the poor's deposits
  - Growing too large for members to know each other: peer monitoring, the whole advantage, disappears
  - Thinking micro-credit is a 20th-century invention: rotating savings clubs are old in Asia and Africa
- History: china: Tang onwards – rotating credit associations (hui) among relatives and neighbours; east_asia: 13th c. – tanomoshi-ko and mujin rotating savings groups in Japan; kye in Korea; africa: rotating savings clubs such as Yoruba esusu, of uncertain antiquity, attested by the 19th c.; europe: 1462 – Monte di Pietà, Perugia (charitable pawnbank); 1778 Hamburg savings fund; 1810 Henry Duncan's Ruthwell Savings Bank; 1844 Rochdale Pioneers; 1850 Schulze-Delitzsch credit unions for artisans; 1864 Raiffeisen's rural credit society at Heddesdorf; india: 1904 – Co-operative Credit Societies Act
- Read:
  - Timothy W. Guinnane, Cooperatives as Information Machines: German Rural Credit Cooperatives, 1883–1914, Journal of Economic History 61 (2001)
  - Johnston Birchall, The International Co-operative Movement (1997)
